walkthroughs.body_html:
When the bases match, indices follow neat rules.

Multiply: aᵐ × aⁿ = aᵐ⁺ⁿ. So 2³ × 2⁴ = 2⁷ = 128.

Divide: aᵐ ÷ aⁿ = aᵐ⁻ⁿ. So 3⁵ ÷ 3² = 3³ = 27.

Power of a power: (aᵐ)ⁿ = aᵐⁿ. So (5²)³ = 5⁶.

Special: a⁰ = 1 (any base ≠ 0). a⁻ⁿ = 1/aⁿ, so 2⁻³ = 1/8.

Standard form writes big or tiny numbers as A × 10ⁿ, where 1 ≤ A < 10.

5 × 10³ = 5000 (move decimal 3 right). 3.2 × 10⁴ = 32000.

Negative powers shrink: 4 × 10⁻² = 0.04 (move decimal 2 left).

Why bother? It keeps massive numbers (mass of the Sun) and tiny ones (size of an atom) tidy.

Write each number in prime factorisation, then:

HCF = product of shared primes (lowest power).

LCM = product of all primes (highest power).

Example: 24 = 2³ × 3 and 36 = 2² × 3². HCF = 2² × 3 = 12. LCM = 2³ × 3² = 72.
